provenance.instrument: Springfield Township (Montgomery County) Code Chapter 114 Zoning (Ord. No. 242, 1940, reenacted Ord. No. 487, 8-8-1962, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 'Includes legislation through 05-13-2026'. New Laws on 2026-11-14: none. The accessory apartment listing in the Historic Resource Overlay District (114-12D4B(10)) was added 12-11-2019 by Ord. No. 962.
checks: The zoning code has no general ADU rule. Each residence district allows the listed uses 'and for no other' (114-41, 114-51, 114-61, 114-71, 114-81, 114-8C1)

Only a property with a historic resource on the Township's Historic Resource Inventory, in the Historic Resource Overlay District, may have an 'accessory apartment': one apartment 'located in a structure accessory to the principal dwelling', by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board after a Historical Commission recommendation. The Board must find the accessory structure a contributing resource listed on the Inventory, the apartment must be the only other dwelling unit, two extra parking spaces are needed and the owner must live on the property (114-12D4B(10), 114-12D6)
The overlay listing reaches the property only where it 'obtains access from any cartway'. Hours limits (12 hours a day between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m.) also name the accessory apartment (114-12D4B, D(3))
Without public sewer a County Health Department permit must show the septic system can take the added load. With public sewer the needed EDUs must be acquired (114-12D4C(7))

Conversion: the Zoning Hearing Board may allow by special exception the conversion of a dwelling that existed when Article XIII took effect into a dwelling for more families in AA, A and B. Lot area per family at least 15,000 sq ft in AA, 8,000 in A and 5,000 in B. No major outside structural change except for sanitation or safety. Only for 'a building which has relatively little economic value or usefulness as a single-family dwelling' (114-133A)

A two-family detached or semidetached dwelling (one family living wholly or partly over the other) is permitted by right in C (5,000 sq ft per family) and D (3,500 sq ft per family) (114-71B, C, 114-72A, 114-81A, 114-82A, 114-21)

Accessory buildings may not exceed 20 ft or one story, whichever is less. One standing in a side yard or the required rear yard must be at least 10 ft behind the rear of the house, 7 ft from the lot line (4 ft if masonry), and at most 12 ft with a sloped roof or 9 ft with a flat roof (114-131B(2), C(2), D)
Parking: two spaces for each housekeeping unit (114-134A(1)). The overlay asks two spaces for the accessory apartment in addition to those for the house (114-12D4B(10)(c))
Where public sewer is not available a lot needs at least 12,500 sq ft unless the Department of Health certifies a smaller area (114-130C)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Springfield Township (Montgomery County) Zoning Officer. Read on eCode360 (SP0463) in a browser, one print view at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search for 'accessory dwelling', 'accessory apartment', 'in-law', ECHO, granny, 'family dwelling', relatives, caretaker, conversion, 'accessory unit' and 'living quarters' found the overlay accessory apartment, the 114-133A conversion, school conversions to offices (114-139.1) and watchmen in the Industrial District (114-121). Use lists read for AAA, AA, A, B, C, D and Multiple Use Residence. The Multifamily Apartment, Cluster Residential, Institutional, B1, B2, Shopping Center, Industrial and Limited Industrial use lists were not read. The search found no ADU-like listing there. Attachment 2 (Summary of Zoning Requirements) was not opened.

term.note: 'One single-family apartment unit located in a structure accessory to the principal dwelling.' Listed only for a historic resource in the Historic Resource Overlay District. The code has no general definition.

status.note: No general ADU rule. The residence districts allow the listed uses 'and for no other'. Only a property with a historic resource in the overlay has an accessory apartment path (special exception, 114-12D4B(10)).

path.note: A second dwelling unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use outside the overlay. It needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). In C and D a two-family dwelling is permitted, and in AA, A and B the Board may allow a conversion by special exception (114-133A).

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

historic_path.note: For a historic resource in the Historic Resource Overlay District, with access from a cartway: an accessory apartment by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board after a Historical Commission recommendation. Owner must live on the property. Conditions in gates.

value.name: Conversion of a dwelling to more families
value.conditions: Conversion of a dwelling that existed when Article XIII took effect into a dwelling for more families. Lot area per family at least 15,000 sq ft in AA, 8,000 in A and 5,000 in B. Yards and building area not reduced. No major outside structural change except for sanitation or safety. Only for a building with relatively little economic value or use as a single-family dwelling. The Board may add conditions.

requires.condition: The dwelling existed at the effective date of Article XIII (the date is not shown in the code text)
A building with relatively little economic value or usefulness as a single-family dwelling

value.note: Lot figures are for two families. The Article XIII effective date is not printed, so the age test is left to the Zoning Officer.

value.name: Two-family detached or semidetached dwelling
value.conditions: A building for two families, one living wholly or partly over the other. Lot area per family: C 5,000 sq ft, D 3,500 sq ft. C side yards 8 ft each, 20 in all. D two-family detached side yards 16 ft each, 35 in all. Two parking spaces per housekeeping unit.
value.note: Read as a path for an existing house converted to two stacked units. 114-130C asks 12,500 sq ft for a lot without public sewer unless the Department of Health certifies less.

zoning_districts.note: No district lists an ADU. The overlay accessory apartment applies over any underlying district, on a historic resource only.

historic_bypass.note: The historic path is its own special exception, not a bypass of district rules.

historic_test.value: The property has a historic resource on the Township's Historic Resource Inventory, in the Historic Resource Overlay District, and access from a cartway
historic_test.note: Confirm the property is on the Inventory and in the overlay with the Zoning Officer.

existing_structure_only.note: Historic path only. The accessory structure must be a contributing resource on the Inventory, so it already exists.

value.condition: A historic resource on the Historic Resource Inventory, in the overlay, with access from a cartway. Historical Commission recommendation and Zoning Hearing Board special exception (114-12D6 criteria, impact study where land development is proposed).
The apartment must be in a structure accessory to the house that the Zoning Hearing Board finds to be a contributing resource identified on the Historic Resource Inventory.
'The accessory apartment shall be the only other dwelling unit on the property.'
'The property owner must reside on the premises.'
Without public sewer, a Montgomery County Department of Health permit showing the septic system can take the added load. With public sewer, documentation that the needed EDUs were acquired.

In a residential district: new parking seen from neighbors screened to 5 ft, one sign of at most 2 sq ft, no noise at the property line, shielded lighting, use hours at most 12 a day between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m.

The district building area, impervious and yard rules may be modified by up to 15% by special exception after a Historical Commission recommendation, more where essential to preserve the resource. Added building area may not exceed 50% of the resource's building area.
A use under the overlay needs a use and occupancy certificate, must be registered with the Zoning Officer within 30 days, and ends if the property no longer has a historic resource.

types_allowed.note: No form is allowed off the historic path.

types_allowed_historic.note: Historic path only: 'located in a structure accessory to the principal dwelling' that is a contributing resource. A unit inside or added to the house and a new building are not named.

value.garage_conversion: In an accessory structure that is a contributing historic resource

max_sqft.note: No size cap for the accessory apartment.

max_height_ft.note: 'Accessory buildings shall not exceed 20 feet or one story in height, whichever is less.' On the historic path the structure already exists.

max_height_stories.note: 20 ft or one story, whichever is less.

value.where: An accessory building in a side yard or the required rear yard
value.note: 12 ft with a sloped roof, 9 ft with a flat roof, or one story, whichever is less. It must be at least 10 ft behind the rear of the house and 7 ft from the side or rear line (4 ft if masonry).

owner_occupancy.note: Historic path only. 'The property owner must reside on the premises.'

family_only.note: No family rule on the historic path.

max_adus.note: Historic path only. 'The only other dwelling unit on the property.'

spaces_required.note: 'Two off-street parking spaces shall be required for the accessory apartment, in addition to the parking spaces necessary for the principal use of the property.'

total_on_site.note: Historic path: 2 for the house ('Two parking spaces for each housekeeping unit') and 2 for the apartment.

min_lot_sqft.note: Cluster lot on a tract of 10 acres or more (10,000 where the underlying district is AA). Standard lots on tracts under 10 acres follow the underlying district.
